questions.html:
Consider the following statements:
S1 : The Fact Constellation Schema increases data redundancy.
S2 : The Fact Constellation Schema reduces the complexity of querying data by merging multiple facts.
Which of the following is correct?
questions.solution:
(a)
• The Fact Constellation Schema increases data redundancy as it contains multiple fact tables
which may result in repeated information across the schema. So, S1 is correct.
• While the schema might simplify some queries by organizing facts more efficiently, it can also
increase the complexity of queries due to the increased number of fact tables. So, S2 is incorrect.

questions.html:
Consider the following statements:
S1 : Dice creates a sub-cube by selecting values from two or more dimensions of the original cube.
S2 : Cubes are a logical representation of multidimensional data used to model complex analytical queries
Which of the following is correct?
questions.solution:
(c)
• The Dice operation is a common OLAP operation that extracts a smaller sub-cube from the
original cube by selecting specific values across two or more dimensions. This allows focused
analysis on a subset of the data while preserving multiple dimensions. So, S1 is correct.
• A cube is a logical representation of multidimensional data, enabling users to model and
analyze complex queries involving several dimensions like time, location, and product
categories. This structure supports efficient data exploration in OLAP systems. So, S2 is correct.

Consider a relation R(A, B, C, D) stored on disk where A is the primary key, B is a foreign key, C
is a non-key attribute in the relation R and data file is physically sorted on attribute C.
Which of the following statements is/are true?

options.html: A primary index can be created on attribute A, but not on attribute C, since C is not unique.
Attribute C can support a clustered index, while A can support a dense index.
Attribute C may form a primary index at the second-level index due to its role in physical ordering.
A B<sup>+</sup> Tree index is well-suited for attribute B if foreign key-based equality and range queries are common.

questions.solution:
(b, d)
• File is not sorted on A so no primary index can built on it. So, option (a) is false.
• The primary index is always the first-level index on the ordering attribute. Second-level indexes
are built on top of it, but they are not called “primary indexes”. So, option (c) is false.

questions.html:
Consider the following statements:
S1 : In an OLAP database, tables are generally denormalized to optimize query performance.
S2 : Normalization in OLAP databases is avoided as it may complicate query execution and slow down performance.
Which of the following is correct?
questions.solution:
(c)
• OLAP databases are generally denormalized to simplify data retrieval and improve query performance. So, S1 is correct.
• Normalization in OLAP databases is avoided because it can lead to more complex queries and
slower performance due to additional joins. So, S2 is correct.

options.html: MOLAP may lead to high storage efficiency when handling sparse datasets due to its cube structure.
Sparse data in MOLAP cubes can result in underutilized storage, affecting overall efficiency.
MOLAP uses pre-aggregated multidimensional cubes, limiting its ability to store detailed transactional data.
MOLAP provides high data granularity, making it ideal for storing detailed transactional records.

questions.solution:
(b, c)
• Sparse datasets often result in low storage efficiency in MOLAP due to unused space in preallocated cube structures. So, option (a) is incorrect.
• Sparse data in MOLAP cubes can result in underutilized storage, affecting overall efficiency.
So, option (b) is correct.
• MOLAP uses pre-aggregated multidimensional cubes, limiting its ability to store detailed
transactional data. So, option (c) is correct.
• MOLAP generally reduces granularity due to pre-aggregation; it is not ideal for detailed transactional data. So, option (d) is incorrect.

questions.html: Which of the following is a characteristic of the Roll-Up operation in OLAP?

options.html: Roll-up aggregates data from lower levels of hierarchy to higher levels.
Roll-up shows detailed data within a specific dimension.
Roll-up splits data into smaller segments based on attributes.
Roll-up deletes unnecessary data points in the hierarchy.

questions.solution:
(a)
Roll-Up refers to summarizing or aggregating data to a higher level of abstraction, such as from monthly data to yearly data.

Which of the following statements is true about the Drill Down and Roll Up operations in OLAP?

options.html: Drill down and roll up are opposite operations, with drill down used for aggregation and roll up used for detailed analysis.
Both drill down and roll up are used to navigate between different levels of data in a hierarchy, but drill down shows more detail and roll up provides higher-level summaries.
Drill down is used only to navigate within the same level of hierarchy, while roll up is used to summarize data from multiple sources.
Drill down and roll up are not related to data hierarchies but are used to filter out unwanted data points.

questions.solution:
(b)
Drill Down and Roll Up are opposite operations used to navigate through a hierarchy: Drill Down provides more detailed data, while Roll Up aggregates data at higher levels.
